newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Detained Bangladesh opposition leaders freed.
newsitem.headline: Detained Bangladesh opposition leaders freed.

text.p: Three opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leaders were freed following weeks of detention after the country's High Court ruled that their arrests were illegal and amounted to political victimisation.
Former ministers Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain and Abdul Mannan and the former Mayor of Dhaka, Mirza Abbas, left jail on Monday night and were greeted by thousands of supporters.
A fourth former minister, Goyeswar Roy, was not released because he faced charges in another case, police said without giving details.

The High Court on Monday ruled that the arrest of the leaders of the BNP, headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, was "illegal, prompted by malafide intention and amounted to political victimisation."
The court ordered the government to release the detainees immediately "if they are not wanted in connection with other cases."

The four were arrested on March 20 and sent to jail under the country's Special Powers Act, which allows for the detention of anyone for up to four months without being charged. Such detentions can be overturned by the High Court on merit.
Official sources at the time said the four were suspected of "inciting acts of sabotage" to destabilise the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
The court also asked the government to pay each of the detainees 100,000 taka ($2,300) in compensation.
The three BNP leaders, garlanded by cheering supporters at the jail gate, met Khaleda shortly after being released, and vowed to continue their "relentless campaign" to bring down the government.
"Now it has proved beyond any doubt that the government is pursuing a vandetta against political rivals," one leader told reporters.
Government attorneys told reporters they would appeal the High Court's ruling to the Supreme Court.
